name: Quarters Apex Adjustment vs 2x2
personnel: Peso Dime (4 DL + 2 LB + Rover + 4 DB)

summary.motive: Give every slot receiver both an underneath apex defender and a matching quarter safety so a two-by-two mesh concept can never isolate anyone or occupy both deep halves.
summary.keyDefender: SS — the strong quarter whose carry rule converts the seam into a double team the moment Y goes vertical
summary.whyItWorks: Quarters pattern-match rules answer every #2 route automatically: vertical gets carried, underneath gets sunk behind, and the apexes play man through the middle while the rover robs the mesh point.
summary.failureMode: Attacking the light box before routes develop — only three linemen and two apex defenders stand between the quarterback and an inside run or quick pressure.

beats.title: 1. Apex Overload on Both Twos
beats.text: Against two-by-two, both apex backers align directly over the slots rather than in B-gaps, giving each #2 receiver an underneath defender plus a matching quarter safety. The tite box stays intact behind them.

beats.title: 2. Seam Meets the Carry Rule
beats.text: The strong slot releases vertical and the strong quarter immediately carries — quarters means the safety takes all vertical #2s. MIKE walls the seam from underneath, building an instant double team.

beats.title: 3. Underneath #2 Sinks the Weak Quarter
beats.text: The weak slot drags under, flipping the weak quarter’s read: #2 under means sink, not chase. He drops to the deep quarter while the apex turns and runs with the crosser man-to-man.

beats.title: 4. The Crosser Runs Into the Rob
beats.text: The quarterback forces the drag a beat late and the ball arrives into a three-defender convergence: trailing apex, robbing peso, sinking quarter behind. Every window the mesh tried to create already had a name on it.

relations.tell: Both linebackers aligned directly OVER the slots at apex depth instead of stacked in the B-gap boxes — the pure quarters-overload picture reserved for two-by-two.
